findings.title: Shared queue pool is shut down when a rebalance closes the old strategy
findings.body: `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` hands the same `self.queue_pool` to every strategy it creates, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` (queue_consumer.py ~lines 335-342) call `queue_pool.shutdown()`. On a Kafka rebalance, arroyo calls `create_with_partitions` again and closes the previous strategy. The old strategy's close shuts down the pool that the new strategy is using. Afterwards `FixedQueuePool.submit` calls `queue.put` on shut-down queues, which raises, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` logs and silently drops the message while marking its offset complete. Result messages are lost after any rebalance. The pool lifetime needs to be owned by the factory, not by each strategy's close().

findings.title: Offsets are committed from a background thread, not the processing thread
findings.body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which is the arroyo `commit` callable bound to the consumer. Arroyo/Kafka consumer commits are not designed to be called concurrently with the consumer's poll loop from another thread, and the strategy's `poll()`/`submit()` run on the processing thread. This can race with the consumer's own commit/poll or with rebalance handling and produce undefined commit behaviour. Commits should be triggered from the strategy's poll/submit path on the processing thread.

findings.title: A single missing offset permanently stalls commits for the partition
findings.body: In `get_committable_offsets`, the loop breaks at the first offset that is not in `all_offsets`. Kafka offsets are not guaranteed contiguous (log compaction, transaction control markers, aborted transactions). If an offset is never delivered to `submit`, `highest_committable` never advances past it, and every later offset is treated as blocked forever. Consumer lag then grows without bound and the committed position never moves, so on restart everything after the gap is reprocessed. The tracker should treat the gap as a non-outstanding position, e.g. by advancing over offsets that were never registered and were below the next delivered offset.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so the advertised backpressure does not exist
findings.body: The class docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but every queue is created with `queue.Queue()` (no maxsize), and `submit` never blocks. The consumer will keep polling and buffering Kafka messages in memory whenever a slow worker falls behind, which can exhaust memory under a backlog. Either bound the queues and block or pause the consumer, or remove the claim from the docstring.

findings.title: Shutdown discards queued work items without draining them
findings.body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets `worker.shutdown = True` before shutting down the queues. The worker loop checks that flag before each `get`, so items still queued are abandoned rather than processed. Their offsets are never committed, so they will be reprocessed later. This is safe for at-least-once delivery, but it is not what the 'no item is lost' guarantee in the strategy docstring implies, and nothing logs how many items were dropped.

findings.title: Rebalance/recreate scenario is not tested, which hides the shared-pool shutdown bug
findings.body: All factory tests create one strategy per factory and shut the factory down at the end. There is no test that calls `create_with_partitions` twice, closes the first strategy, and then submits to the second. Such a test would expose that closing one strategy shuts down the shared queue pool and drops messages.

findings.title: Error-handling test assertion is too weak to verify offset behaviour
findings.body: `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` passes whether or not the failed message blocks the commit. The test also says it checks that errors 'don't block offset commits for other messages', but it never asserts the committed offset for the successful message (101), so it cannot detect the regression it names.

findings.title: `pytestmark` on a unittest TestCase class is ineffective and the Kafka test may silently skip or leak topics
findings.body: `pytestmark = [requires_kafka]` is set on a Django/unittest `TestCase` subclass, where pytest markers are not reliably applied, so the test can run without Kafka and fail with an unhelpful error. The `finally` block also swallows all exceptions from `delete_topics` with a bare `except Exception: pass`, so topic cleanup failures go unnoticed.
